newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET CONTINUES LIQUID, RATES LOW.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET CONTINUES LIQUID, RATES LOW.

text.p: Zimbabwe's money market continued liquid on Wednesday on the back of maturing treasury bills with short-term trading rates mixed to lower.
"The market is very liquid from treasury bills maturing and some inflows of foreign exchange. Rates are on the low side," one dealer said.
The dealers said discount houses were taking up treasury bills at 16.23 percent from 16.30 percent previously and selling them in the secondary market at 16.15 percent from 16.25 percent.

NCDs with maturity of 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought and sold at 17.50 percent and 16.75 percent respectively versus 17 percent and 16.75 percent while the rates for bankers acceptances were indicated at 16.85 percent (buying) and 16.30 percent (selling) compared to 16.75 percent and 16.50 percent.
Call money slipped to 16 percent from 16.25 percent in a market which closed Tuesday with a surplus of Z$38.1 million.
